Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: ONE square production texture atlas for a wood material renderer, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows, nine equal square cells, edge to edge, no gutters, borders, labels, text, tools or objects. Output high resolution 2048 by 2048 or greater. Each cell is a directly overhead, orthographic close-up of a DIFFERENT smoothly sanded wood surface with a light clear-oil finish, evenly diffuse neutral studio lighting and detailed natural pores. These are original illustrative wood textures, not copies of stock photographs. No perspective, boards' outer edges, metal, brush marks or specular hotspots. Long grain flows vertically top to bottom where applicable. Keep every cell's appearance contained within its grid square; no blending into its neighbours. Natural material variation, not a cartoon pattern. CELL ORDER, left to right then top to bottom: Row 1: (1) Indian rosewood, chocolate brown with irregular narrow dark streaks and open pores; (2) ebony, nearly black warm brown, extremely fine subtle longitudinal grain, still visibly wood; (3) wenge, deep coffee brown with dense straight black streaks and lighter narrow brown pores. Row 2: (4) ironwood, warm golden honey-brown and dark chocolate interlocked flowing grain with wood chatoyance, definitely organic WOOD not metallic iron, no grey metal; (5) bog oak, dark charcoal-brown with visibly porous straight oak grain and understated medullary flecks; (6) snakewood, reddish chestnut with distinctive small irregular near-black mottled flecks arranged along the grain, organic viper-like figure, not literal snakeskin. Row 3: (7) wamara, medium dark reddish-brown to plum-brown with darker contrasting longitudinal stripes; (8) kingwood, rich violet-brown with fine dark and lighter purple-brown streaks; (9) African blackwood, very dark purple-black fine close wood grain with a few subtle warm-brown streaks. Distinct realistic timber surfaces, moderate contrast so the grain remains visible on a guitar fingerboard.
